descriptionAdvanced.en: Puerto Jennifer is a state-of-the-art private river terminal located on the Tamengo Canal, near Puerto Quijarro in eastern Bolivia. In 2018, it achieved the historic milestone of being designated as an International Port, providing Bolivia with a high-capacity, sovereign gateway to the Atlantic Ocean via the Paraguay-Paraná Waterway. The port is specifically designed for the efficient export of massive volumes of soy, sunflowers, and other grains, as well as minerals and industrial cargo. It features advanced loading technology and large-scale storage facilities, significantly reducing the country's dependence on Pacific ports in Chile and Peru. Puerto Jennifer is a key strategic asset in Bolivia's 'Turn to the East' economic strategy, positioning the nation as a vital hub for regional trade in the heart of South America.

en: Puerto Jennifer can handle up to 2 million tons of cargo annually.
It is the first private port in Bolivia to receive international status from the national maritime authority.
The port operates year-round, utilizing the dredging and maintenance of the Tamengo Canal.
It is strategically linked to the 'Bi-Oceanic Railway' that connects the Atlantic and Pacific coasts.
